title: Diagnosing Low-Confidence Patient Profiles via Localized Harmful Covariate Shift Detection
description: MED3pa first discovers interpretable low-confidence patient profiles, and Detectron is then applied within each profile to test whether its degradation is associated with a detectable harmful covariate shift. An injected age shift, undetectable at the population level, was nonetheless localized to specific degraded profiles …

paper.authors: Olivier Lefebvre, Hakima Laribi, Dan Poenaru, Martin Vallières

example_outputs.title: Default inputs
example_outputs.summary: The age shift was missed at population level (p = 0.19). Two of five profiles were flagged; in the largest, AUC fell from 0.69 to 0.64. A synthetic MIMIC-like cohort replaces MIMIC-IV. Detectron is simplified; borderline profiles change with the seed.

inputs.label: Dataset
inputs.description: synthetic (100,000-patient MIMIC-like readmission cohort with known mechanisms) or diabetes130 (UCI Diabetes 130-US hospitals, real, ~3 MB download)

inputs.label: Removed subgroup
inputs.description: Subgroup removed from training only: age<50, sex (female removed), race (non-White removed)

inputs.label: Tree depth
inputs.description: Depth of MED3pa's profile tree (2–4); deeper = more, smaller profiles

inputs.label: CDCs
inputs.description: Constrained disagreement classifiers per Detectron test (2–10)

inputs.label: Detectron sample
inputs.description: Max deployment (and reference) cases per Detectron test (50–1000)

inputs.label: Detectron repeats
inputs.description: Independent repeats per test; HCS if median p < α (1–9)

inputs.label: Min profile share
inputs.description: Smallest profile tested (paper: 5% of the population)

inputs.label: Seed
inputs.description: Seed for the split, models and (synthetic) cohort
